Two suspected kidnappers have been shot dead in a gun duel with operatives of the Delta State Police Command. PUNCH Metro learnt that the incident followed the abduction of a 30-year-old man (name withheld) on November 12, 2026, in Edo-Ogwashi. Operatives of the Special Anti-Kidnapping Unit, Sector III, Ubulu-Uku, in collaboration with a human rights activist and members of the Ubulu-Uku community vigilante group, acting on intelligence, trailed the suspected kidnappers to their hideout in the Edo-Ogwashi forest on November 15, 2026, at about 7am. The hoodlums, on sighting the security team, immediately opened fire on them. The team, however, engaged the suspected kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. In the ensuing exchange of gunfire, two of the suspects sustained gunshot injuries, while others escaped. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The state Police Public Relations Officer for the Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, confirmed the incident, saying that “one locally fabricated single-barrel gun, three live cartridges and part of the ransom paid were recovered.” The PPRO added that “the injured suspects were taken to the hospital, where they were confirmed dead by the doctor.” According to the police spokesman, “a manhunt for the other fleeing suspects is ongoing.” Bandits kill one, abduct five family members in fresh Zamfara attack Delta proposes N1.23tn 2027 budget, vows no borrowing AGF risks jail over detained Okuama leaders – Court In another development, on Sunday, at about 3:30pm, operatives of the Agbor Division, while conducting a stop-and-search operation along Baleke Street, Agbor, intercepted one Lucky Rechard, aged 31. A search of the suspect led to the recovery of one English pistol, one locally made cut-to-size gun and three live cartridges. The PPRO confirmed that the suspect was in custody, while investigations were ongoing. Meanwhile, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Erale, commended members of the public “for volunteering credible information” and appreciated the continued collaboration of community vigilante groups, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in combating crime. The CP reiterated the importance of community policing and urged citizens to “sustain this partnership with the police in the collective interest of peace and security across the State.” Dele Ogunyemi Dele Ogunyemi is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over 25 years of experience in media practice.
